notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: Thin, slightly curved bollards with a rectangular front reflector and two round ones on the back, white or orange; numbers often sit below the front.

notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Long white plates with the blue EU strip on the left.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Pole tops with hook-shaped insulators alternating left-right-left; much rarer in the other two Baltic states.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Pedestrian sign has five stripes and a long-legged figure; the other Baltic states use three stripes.

notes.subject: street
notes.text: The bus stop sign shows a bus with five windows; the other two Baltic states show four.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Warning and speed signs have a thick red border with a thin white outline around it.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Blue kilometre markers sit parallel to the road and carry a number on one side only.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Chevrons are white with red arrows, as in Lithuania and Poland. Estonia, Russia and Ukraine use red with white arrows.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Direction signs are blue with white text, and the arrow is more stylised than the vertical-backed ones next door.

notes.subject: guardrail
notes.text: Ordinary A-type guardrails with white or red reflectors. Estonia has none; Lithuania uses orange.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: Macron vowels Ā Ē Ī and hooked consonants Ģ Ķ Ļ Ņ are unique among the Baltic languages.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: The word for street is "iela", unique to this language. Rarely "gatve" shows up in the capital, as in Lithuania.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: House numbers are often tall rectangles in various colours, uncommon in neighbouring Estonia and Lithuania.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Wood combined with white brick under steep corrugated metal roofs; pastel stone houses are also common.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: Red and black Generation 4 cars appear; both also occur in Lithuania but not in Estonia.

notes.subject: vegetation
notes.text: South of Jelgava the land is wide open, with far fewer forests and more fields than elsewhere.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: The historic centre of the capital is full of grand art nouveau buildings, like Vienna; unique in the Baltics.
